== Biography ==
'''William Glasgow''' was born around 1855, in "Old Cowit," County Cork, Ireland, to [[Glasgow-971|Alexander Glasgow]] and [[Smith-228705|Ellen Smith]]. His parents were originally from Barony, Lanark, Scotland, where they had at least two children: Janet, born circa April 1829, and William James, born on May 28, 1831.

In search of new opportunities, William settled in Suburban North, near Nelson, New Zealand. He became an indentured servant through an agreement made on July 30, 1855. This indenture involved several parties: his father, Alexander Glasgow; William himself; Bernard Robert Shaw; William's future wife, Dora Shaw (née Shaw); Edward Eyre Newenham; and Eyre Massey Shaw.

William married Dora Shaw, further solidifying his ties to the Shaw family and the community in New Zealand.

Sadly, William passed away in 1886 at the age of 54 in Suburban North, Nelson, New Zealand. His death is documented in the "New Zealand, Archives New Zealand, Probate Records, 1843-1998" and the New Zealand Births Deaths and Marriages Online with the Death Registration number: 1886/5271.

It is noted that William was the junior son of the late Alexander Glasgow, a merchant from Tullyveagh, Tyrone, who died on November 17, 1866, at Cloghog. This piece of information connects William to the broader Glasgow family history, highlighting the family's origins and movements.
